Question: What exactly is Simple Mining proposing to build and operate at the Cascade site, and what services or computing workloads do you currently expect the facility to support?
Is this facility being designed specifically for Bitcoin or cryptocurrency mining, or could it also host AI, high-performance computing, cloud computing, colocation, or other data-center customers?
Who will own the Cascade facility, who will operate it, and which legal entity will ultimately be responsible for complying with agreements made with the City of Cascade?
What is the proposed size of the initial facility in square feet, and what is the maximum size the site could reach if fully developed?
Is the project expected to be constructed in phases? If so, what are the anticipated phases, sizes, and approximate timelines?
What is the expected average electrical demand of the initial Cascade facility in megawatts, and what is the expected maximum or peak demand?
What would the electrical demand be if the Cascade site were fully built out to its maximum planned capacity?
What utility, substation, transmission, generation, or distribution upgrades will be required to serve the facility?
Who will pay for electrical infrastructure upgrades required specifically because of this project?
Can Simple Mining commit that Cascade residents and other existing utility customers will not be required to subsidize infrastructure constructed primarily to serve this facility?
Will the facility participate in utility demand-response or curtailment programs during periods of unusually high electrical demand, and if so, how would those programs work?
What specific cooling technology is proposed for the Cascade facility?
Will the computing equipment use closed-loop liquid cooling, air cooling, evaporative cooling, immersion cooling, or some combination of these systems?
What is the estimated average daily water consumption for the initial Cascade facility?
What is the estimated maximum daily water consumption during the hottest operating conditions?
What is the estimated annual water consumption at initial operation and at maximum buildout?
What source will supply water to the facility, and would any water be obtained from Cascade's municipal water system or local groundwater?
Will the facility use potable municipal water for cooling or other industrial purposes?
What happens to water after it is used by the facility, including any wastewater, blowdown, discharge, or treatment?
What chemicals, if any, will be added to cooling or water-treatment systems, and how will those chemicals be stored and disposed of?
What measures would Simple Mining take to reduce water consumption during drought, water shortages, or unusually hot conditions?
What is the predicted continuous noise level in dBA at the property line during normal operation?
What is the predicted noise level at the nearest existing residence during normal daytime and nighttime operation?
Has Simple Mining performed or commissioned an acoustical model for the Cascade site? If so, will the complete report be made available to the public?
Will the noise study evaluate tonal noise and low-frequency noise in addition to the overall A-weighted dBA level?
What cooling fans, transformers, generators, pumps, or other equipment are expected to be the major sources of continuous noise?
Is Simple Mining willing to accept an enforceable property-line noise limit, including separate nighttime requirements?
Is Simple Mining willing to fund independent post-construction noise measurements performed by a qualified third party selected or approved by the City?
If post-construction testing shows that the facility exceeds an agreed noise limit, what specific corrective actions would Simple Mining be willing to take?
How many backup generators are currently anticipated for the Cascade facility, what type and size would they be, and what fuel would they use?
How often would backup generators normally be tested, during what hours, and approximately how long would each test last?
What noise levels and air emissions are expected from backup generator operation?
Is Simple Mining willing to pay for an independent environmental impact assessment of the Cascade project performed by a qualified third party acceptable to the City?
What effects could the proposed facility have on stormwater runoff, drainage, erosion, groundwater, or nearby surface water?
What waste streams will the facility generate, including electronic waste, batteries, oils, coolants, chemicals, filters, or other industrial materials?
How will waste electronics and failed computing equipment be recycled or disposed of?
What heat will be rejected into the surrounding environment, and has Simple Mining evaluated whether the facility could create measurable localized heat impacts?
How many temporary construction jobs are expected to be created by the Cascade project?
How many permanent full-time equivalent employees are expected to work at the Cascade facility after normal operations begin?
What types of permanent positions will be located in Cascade, and what salary or wage ranges are expected for those positions?
Will Simple Mining commit to recruiting locally for permanent jobs when qualified candidates are available?
Would Simple Mining participate in workforce-development or technical-training partnerships with local schools, community colleges, or other Iowa educational institutions?
What is the estimated taxable value of the completed Cascade facility at initial operation?
What is the estimated annual property-tax contribution to local taxing authorities at initial operation and at full buildout?
What tax abatements, tax increment financing, rebates, grants, infrastructure assistance, or other public incentives has Simple Mining requested or expects to request?
If public incentives are requested, would Simple Mining accept clawback provisions if promised investment, employment, or operational commitments are not met?
What road construction or improvements will be necessary for construction and long-term operation of the facility?
Who would pay for any road, sewer, water, electrical, communications, drainage, or other public infrastructure improvements required primarily by the project?
How much additional truck traffic is expected during construction and during normal operation?
What fire suppression system is proposed for the data center?
Will the facility contain lithium-ion battery energy-storage or UPS systems, and if so, what type and approximate capacity?
What hazardous materials or fuels will normally be stored on site?
What specialized training, equipment, or staffing would Cascade-area fire, EMS, or law-enforcement agencies need in order to respond safely to an emergency at the facility?
Will Simple Mining pay for specialized emergency-response training or equipment required specifically because of the facility?
What physical security measures are proposed for the site, including fencing, cameras, access controls, and security personnel?
What exterior lighting is proposed, and will lighting be shielded or directed to prevent unnecessary light trespass onto neighboring properties?
What project commitments is Simple Mining willing to have incorporated into legally enforceable zoning conditions or a development agreement rather than leaving them as voluntary promises?

If the facility later changes from cryptocurrency mining to AI, high-performance computing, cloud computing, or another workload, could that materially change its electricity, water, cooling, noise, generator, or staffing requirements?
Is Simple Mining willing to notify the City before making a major change in computing workload or equipment that materially changes the facility's physical impacts?

What agreements or negotiations currently exist between Simple Mining and electric utilities, property owners, economic-development organizations, government agencies, or other parties concerning the Cascade project?
Will Simple Mining make non-confidential engineering studies concerning noise, water, electricity, traffic, environmental impact, and emergency response available to the public?
Are there any nondisclosure agreements affecting what Cascade officials, utilities, economic-development organizations, or other parties may publicly disclose about this project?
What existing Simple Mining facility is most comparable in size, technology, electrical demand, cooling system, and surrounding land use to the proposed Cascade facility?
Can Simple Mining provide addresses of comparable operating facilities so Cascade residents and officials can independently evaluate their actual noise, water use, employment, and community impacts?

Have any Simple Mining-operated facilities received documented complaints or regulatory violations involving noise, water, environmental impacts, electrical service, fire safety, or neighboring property impacts?
Who will be the community contact for complaints or concerns once the Cascade facility is operating?
Will Simple Mining establish a documented complaint process with response deadlines and records that can be reviewed by the City?
Will Simple Mining support ongoing public reporting of actual electricity consumption, water consumption, noise compliance, and other agreed environmental or operational metrics?
Would Simple Mining permit independent inspections or compliance testing when the City has a reasonable basis to investigate a possible violation?
What is the expected useful life of the Cascade facility?
What is Simple Mining's plan for removing computing equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, generators, fuel systems, and other improvements if the facility permanently closes?
Is Simple Mining willing to provide a decommissioning bond, letter of credit, escrow account, or other financial assurance so taxpayers are not responsible for cleanup if the facility is abandoned?
How would Simple Mining address documented impacts to neighboring properties if operation of the facility causes noise, drainage, lighting, traffic, or other effects beyond agreed limits?
What do you believe are the three most important benefits this specific project will provide to Cascade residents, excluding benefits that would occur only during temporary construction?
What do you believe are the three most significant potential negative impacts of this specific project, and what concrete measures will Simple Mining take to mitigate each one?
Of the commitments Simple Mining makes at this community forum, which ones is the company willing to put into a written development agreement enforceable by the City of Cascade?
